checks.invariant: Every image upload is rejected unless content-type is in {png,jpeg,gif,webp} AND magic bytes match the declared format AND Pillow can fully decode it.
checks.result: Holds. validate_image_file (storage.py:435-450) enforces size cap, content-type allowlist (_IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES, storage.py:60-65), 16-byte head signature per ext (PNG/JPEG/GIF/WebP RIFF+WEBP). imaging._open does upload.seek(0)+Image.open+image.load() and converts UnidentifiedImageError/DecompressionBombError/OSError/ValueError to ValueError. SVG/ZIP/other formats cannot pass the content-type gate; a mismatched body fails either the signature check or Pillow decode.

checks.invariant: All persisted web images are re-encoded to WebP (EXIF-corrected, size-clamped, alpha only for logo) — no original bytes, polyglots, scripts, or metadata survive.
checks.result: Holds for every persisted path: normalize_image always returns ('webp','image/webp') via _encode (WEBP method=6, quality 78/72, <=350KB target floor q60); exif_transpose applied in _open; non-logo kinds convert to RGB/RGBA and drop EXIF/GPS on save; animated GIF/WebP collapse to first frame; output dims <=1600-2200px per kind. Callers: upload_logo/cover/carousel/gallery/decor/product/brand, chat (attachments.py:36), proof (public.py:236), feed image (feed.py:146), changelog (viewset.py:152), AI design (ai_design.py:3128), remove-background preview is NOT persisted. Exception: feed video is raw bytes by design — see hardening.

checks.invariant: Object keys are server-generated, tenant-scoped, and not injectable or client-writable; no filename/traversal reaches the key.
checks.result: Holds. Keys are f'stores/{store.id}/{folder}/{uuid4().hex}.{ext}', 'chat/{thread.id}/{uuid}.webp', 'changelog/{uuid}.{ext}', 'system/offers/{slug}/{uuid}.webp'. No serializer exposes image_key/media_key/logo_key/cover_key/label_key as writable. 'kind' validated against StoreGalleryImage.KINDS. default_storage.save uses uuid names — no collision/traversal.

checks.invariant: Chat attachments are never publicly fetchable: private bucket objects get short-lived signed URLs only to thread owner/staff; local fallback lives under a prefix nginx refuses to serve.
checks.result: Holds. R2 path: key 'chat/<thread>/<uuid>.webp' -> object_url(private=True, expires=3600) -> presigned SigV4, public base ignored. Local path: key 'private/chat/...' via default_storage; nginx 'location ^~ /media/private/ { return 404; }' precedes '/media/' on BOTH vhosts; Django static() media serving exists only under settings.DEBUG. Attachment endpoint enforces IsAuthenticated + chat_enabled + owner-or-staff, serves local files via default_storage.open(image_key) with DB-sourced key (no traversal), redirects to fresh 1h presigned URL otherwise. chat_image_url always private=True.

checks.invariant: Payment proofs are private objects: signed URLs only, first-write-wins, quota-accounted, released on unpaid close; public tracking never exposes the proof URL.
checks.result: Mostly holds. Upload requires valid tracking_token + PENDING_PAYMENT + non-MP + no existing proof; validate+normalize->WebP; _check_quota fast-path then Store->Order select_for_update recheck; orphan _delete_object on failure; response object_url(key, private=True). Owner serializer get_proof_image uses private=True; public tracking payload exposes only proof_uploaded bool. release_proof deletes row+object+frees quota inside the locking atomic on EXPIRE/CANCEL. Residual: presigned TTL defaults to 7 days vs chat's deliberate 1h — hardening, not a break.

checks.invariant: Upload/delete endpoints resolve the store strictly from the authenticated owner; no cross-tenant object or row access (IDOR).
checks.result: Holds. Store actions use get_object_or_404(Store, user__user=request.user) and child rows scoped store=store. Catalog querysets all filter store=view.my_store(); brand/product image actions go through get_object()/owner queryset. Feed post media scoped get_object_or_404(FeedPost, pk, store=store). Order proof is token-scoped to the store. Public pattern ?product= lookup filters store+is_active+not is_exclusive. Deletes take the key from the locked row, never caller input.

checks.invariant: Storage quota (max_storage_mb) and image-count caps are enforced atomically: fast-path check, PUT, then recheck under select_for_update on the Store row; failed transactions delete the orphaned object; deletes free quota.
checks.result: Holds for all store-scoped uploads. Pattern: validate->normalize->_check_image_slot/_check_quota fast-path->_put_object->atomic{Store select_for_update->recheck->write key+size->_consume_quota}->except ValueError _delete_object(key). Deletes lock Store, clear key/size, _consume_quota(freed), then _delete_object post-commit. release_proof mirrors it for proofs. Exceptions: chat attachments consume NO quota (candidate); changelog has no quota by design (platform asset, staff-only) and has a minor replace race -> orphan.

checks.invariant: Pattern markup served as document/srcdoc cannot execute attacker JS: handlers, scripts, dangerous URL schemes, base/meta/embeds removed; document CSP allows only nonce'd scripts in an opaque-origin sandbox.
checks.result: Holds with defense in depth. sanitize_markup strips <script>, on*= handlers with any quote/unquoted form, javascript:/vbscript:/data:text/html in 10 URL attributes incl. entity/whitespace-obfuscated schemes, <base>/<object>/<embed>/<iframe>/<frame>/<frameset>, and ALL <meta>. sanitize_css removes </style breakouts. pattern_document normalizes theme/surface/style attrs, escapes preload URLs, per-response validated nonce. View sets X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN + document_csp(nonce): default-src 'none', script-src 'nonce-…' (no unsafe-inline), object-src 'none', base-uri 'none', form-action 'none', connect-src 'none'. Preview token = TimestampSigner TTL 3d bound to store.pk. Even if sanitizer missed markup, CSP nonce + opaque origin block script; residual <link>/<style> are staff-authored catalog content neutralized by style-src 'unsafe-inline' — hardening note only.

checks.invariant: Local MEDIA_ROOT fallback cannot expose private objects in production; nginx media handling matches the storage layout.
checks.result: Holds. Django serves MEDIA_URL only when DEBUG; production media is nginx alias /srv/media <- media_data volume <- /app/media. Only two default_storage writers exist: chat attachments under 'private/' (nginx 404 + authed endpoint) and AI-design gallery images under 'stores/<id>/gallery/' which are public-by-design. Store-scoped R2 helpers require store_storage_configured() — no silent local fallback for proofs/changelog/feed (put_object raises ValueError without backend). proofs/changelog keys can never be served from /media/ because they are never written to default_storage.

checks.invariant: BYO storage: owner-supplied endpoint cannot become SSRF; credentials are write-only/encrypted; URL generation resolves the correct bucket per key; public_base_url cannot inject non-https or dangerous schemes.
checks.result: Holds. validate_endpoint enforces https (http only when settings.DEBUG) + host suffix allowlist. bucket regex + region default 'auto'. access_key/secret_key write-only, encrypted via vault purpose per store. _byo_backend requires enabled+endpoint+bucket+both decryptable creds else falls back to DAVENT; _store_id_from_key scopes BYO to 'stores/<id>/...' keys only — chat/changelog/system keys always DAVENT. object_url(private=True) ignores public_base_url -> presigned with owner creds when BYO. public_base_url is arbitrary https — owner could point image URLs at any host, but SPA CSP img-src https: already permits that; no new capability.

checks.invariant: Feed media uploads are owner-scoped, quota-accounted, and image media is normalized; public feed serves only published posts of enabled stores.
checks.result: Partially holds — image path is correct (validate_image_file->normalize_image 'gallery'->WebP, quota fast-path+locked recheck, old media deleted, post delete frees quota+object, owner-scoped 404s, has_feed gate). DEFECT: video branch sets processed=None then calls _put_object which does _IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES[upload.content_type] -> KeyError for 'video/mp4|webm|quicktime' -> uncaught (view catches only ValueError) -> HTTP 500 on every video upload (feed.py:149-160 + storage.py:322-324). Feature is broken, not exploitable — hardening. Also no container/magic-byte validation would exist even if the crash were fixed (content-type only, up to 120MB raw).

checks.invariant: Upload endpoints have effective rate bounds so a single principal cannot amplify storage/CPU cost without limit.
checks.result: Mostly holds: chat_send 120/h, store_order_proof 10/h/IP, store_order_create 10/h, bg_removal 60/h, ai_design_image 60/h, store_review 10/h; XFF-spoof pinned via _pinned_ident. Throttles are deliberately fail-open on cache outage — documented; captcha still gates order creation. GAP: chat attachments have no storage-quota consumption at all (candidate) — only the hourly throttle + annual purge bound total bytes.

checks.invariant: Decompression bombs, animated/polyglot payloads, and orphaned objects are bounded: pixel cap enforced, single-frame output, failed transactions clean up, lifecycle deletes remove objects.
checks.result: Mostly holds: Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS=40M + DecompressionBombError->ValueError; output always single-frame WebP; orphan cleanup on ValueError across all helpers; purge_personal_data deletes chat attachments (R2 via _delete_object or local) for messages older than --days. Residuals (hardening): 40M pixels ~=160MB RGBA transient decode per request is generous vs <=2200px output; _open misses non-standard Pillow exceptions -> 500; chat send uploads object before send_message (DB failure -> orphan); changelog replace race can orphan; _delete_object BYO-first early return can skip the DAVENT delete for fallback-uploaded objects.

candidates.title: Support-chat image attachments bypass plan storage quota — unbounded R2 growth per paid user
candidates.description: Every other image upload in the codebase consumes the store's plan quota (storage_used_bytes under select_for_update) or is a bounded staff/platform asset. Chat attachments are the sole exception: upload_chat_image validates, normalizes to WebP and PUTs the object to the DAVENT R2 bucket (key 'chat/<thread.id>/<uuid>.webp'), but never calls _check_quota/_consume_quota and ChatMessage stores only image_key — no byte accounting anywhere. The only bounds are the chat_send throttle (120/hour per user, itself fail-open when the cache is down) and the annual purge_personal_data cron (default --days 365). A user on any paid plan with has_support_chat can therefore accumulate ~350KB-1MB of WebP per message, up to ~120/hour, indefinitely — gigabytes of operator-owned R2 storage and bucket growth with zero quota enforcement, while sibling uploads are hard-capped by max_storage_mb.
candidates.root_cause: upload_chat_image (AdminApp/domains/chat/services/attachments.py:27-45) performs validate_image_file + normalize_image + put_object but contains no quota check or accounting call; chat keys ('chat/...') do not match _STORE_KEY_RE so they always land in the DAVENT bucket outside store.storage_used_bytes; no per-user/per-thread attachment cap exists in send_message or the viewset.
candidates.intended_behavior: All client-driven object uploads should consume a bounded, plan- or user-scoped storage budget consistent with the quota model used by store images, proofs, feed media and AI-design images — or an equivalent explicit aggregate cap with prompt lifecycle cleanup.

trace.description: POST /api/chat/send/ — IsAuthenticated + _gate(chat_enabled) + ChatSendThrottle(scope chat_send 120/hour); accepts multipart 'image' FileField via ChatSendSerializer (no size field — validate_image_file caps at 4MB later).

upload_chat_image: validate_image_file(upload) -> imaging.normalize_image(upload,'chat') -> key=f'chat/{thread.id}/{uuid4().hex}.{ext}' -> storage.put_object(key, body, content_type) when storage_configured() else default_storage.save('private/'+key). NO quota call.
put_object: _byo_backend_for_key('chat/...') -> _STORE_KEY_RE '^stores/(\d+)/' does not match -> DAVENT bucket; PUT with CacheControl 'private, max-age=0'; raises ValueError only on total failure.
send_message persists ChatMessage.image_key (CharField) — the object key only; no size/quota fields, no FK-level storage accounting.
Only cleanup path: deletes ChatMessage rows + attachments older than --days (default 365) — annual cron, not a real-time bound; active threads' attachments persist indefinitely.

candidates.evidence: attachments.py:27-45 contains zero references to _check_quota/_consume_quota/storage_used_bytes; storage.py:109-116 shows chat keys bypass BYO/store accounting entirely; settings.py:121 sets chat_send='120/hour' as the sole rate bound; grep confirms _check_quota callers are all store-scoped helpers + order proofs — chat is the only unaccounted client upload.
candidates.conditions: Authenticated platform user with a paid plan granting has_support_chat; sustained automated uploads at <=120/hour; R2 (DAVENT bucket) configured — the normal production path.

execution.command: n/a — read-only source audit; no live requests permitted
execution.observed: Static trace: each accepted upload produces a ~350KB (quality floor 60, 1600px cap) WebP object in R2 'chat/<thread>/<uuid>.webp' with no decrement/increment of any quota counter; ChatMessage rows accumulate until the annual purge.

candidates.remediation: Add a bounded budget for chat attachments: e.g., count attachment bytes in a per-user or per-plan quota (extend storage_used_bytes accounting or a dedicated ChatAttachmentUsage table checked+consumed under lock in upload_chat_image), cap total attachments per thread/user, shorten purge retention for attachments, or make the chat_send throttle fail-closed for the send scope.

severity.rationale: Requires a paid account and sustained automation to matter; per-upload output is capped ~350KB-1MB and throttled 120/hour (~40-120MB/hour/user worst case). Impact is operator-owned R2 storage spend and unbounded bucket growth — real but small-dollar and slow; no cross-tenant data exposure.

candidates.confidence: high — missing bound is fully source-visible; only the dollar magnitude depends on deployment volume/pricing.

hardening.detail: upload_post_media video branch (feed/services/feed.py:149-160) passes processed=None to _put_object, which evaluates _IMAGE_CONTENT_TYPES[upload.content_type] (storage.py:322-324) -> KeyError for 'video/mp4|webm|quicktime' -> uncaught -> HTTP 500 on EVERY video upload (view catches only ValueError, feed/views/views.py:141-144). Feature is broken. If fixed, note there is still no container/magic-byte validation — only client content-type + 120MB size cap; add a dedicated video put path plus a lightweight container sniff (ftyp box for mp4/mov, EBML for webm) before persisting raw bytes.

object_url(key, private=True) with no expires -> PRESIGNED_TTL_SECONDS = 7 days (storage.py:53,248-253). Payment proofs are sensitive financial documents; chat attachments deliberately use 1h (attachments.py:21). The 7-day bearer URL is returned in the anonymous upload response (orders/views/public.py:279) and embedded in the owner order-detail payload on every fetch (orders/serializers/serializers.py:164-170). Consider a short TTL (e.g., 1h) for proofs — URLs are regenerated per response anyway — and note campaign label_url uses the same 7-day private URL inside public catalog payloads (catalog/serializers/serializers.py:53,103; catalog/views/viewset.py:246) which is a functional expiry quirk more than a leak.

Image.MAX_IMAGE_PIXELS = 40,000,000 (imaging.py:28): a <=4MB compressed input can still decode to ~40MP ~= 160MB RGBA transient per request on synchronous gunicorn workers, plus WebP encode — while every output is clamped to <=2200px, so inputs beyond ~12-25MP add no quality. Consider lowering the cap (e.g., 20-25MP) to cut worst-case worker memory/CPU; authenticated+throttled so impact is bounded.

_open catches only UnidentifiedImageError, DecompressionBombError, OSError, ValueError (imaging.py:59). Other Pillow failure modes (SyntaxError, IndexError, struct.error, MemoryError on extreme inputs) propagate as 500s. Broadening to Exception (still returning INVALID_IMAGE) would harden the public proof endpoint and all upload actions against malformed-file crashes.

remove_background returns PNG bytes ('png','image/png', imaging.py:255-276) served as a one-off preview HttpResponse (catalog/views/viewset.py:335-338). It is NOT persisted — the client re-uploads through upload_product_image->normalize_image->WebP — so no invariant break, but the ~1000x1000 PNG preview is heavier than needed and deviates from the repo's WebP-only image rule; encoding the preview as WebP would align policy and save bandwidth.

notifications image action reads old=entry.image_key before put_object+save (AdminApp/domains/notifications/views/viewset.py:138-156) with no row lock/transaction: two concurrent staff uploads can orphan the loser's object (no quota impact — platform asset). Wrap in transaction.atomic with select_for_update on the entry.

_delete_object tries the BYO backend first and returns on success (storage.py:267-273); S3 delete of a nonexistent key returns success, so when an upload fell back to the DAVENT bucket during a BYO outage, the DAVENT copy is never deleted -> orphaned bytes (documented MVP limitation, storage.py:37-45). Attempting DAVENT delete unconditionally (best-effort both) would close the leak.

viewset.send uploads the attachment (R2 PUT / local save) before send_message; a DB failure in send_message leaves an unreferenced object (AdminApp/domains/chat/views/viewset.py:141-153). Wrap send_message and _delete_object(image_key)/default_storage.delete on failure.

All Resilient* throttles fail open on cache outage (DaventProject/throttling.py:64-79, deliberate). Upload-cost bounds (chat_send, store_order_proof, ai_design_image, bg_removal) therefore depend on Redis availability; captcha still gates order creation. Consider a fail-closed or degraded-mode cap for the highest-cost scopes (proof/chat_send) if abuse during outages is a concern.

sanitize_markup does not strip <link> or <style> elements (pattern_document.py:322-335). External <link rel=stylesheet> is blocked by CSP style-src 'unsafe-inline' and scripts are nonce-gated, so impact is nil today — but pattern.html/css/js are staff-authored catalog content interpolated with store data; adding <link>/<style> to the denylist (or allowlisting known CDN hosts) would reduce reliance on CSP alone. Source-document ASSET_RE preserves external <script src>/<link> into pattern.html at import (source_document.py:24-44) — scripts are later stripped at serve time, links survive.

purge_personal_data defaults to --days 365 and only runs if scheduled; combined with the missing quota (candidate) this is the sole retention bound for chat attachments. Consider a shorter attachment-specific retention and/or per-thread caps.

uncovered: R2 bucket public-access configuration: whether R2_PUBLIC_URL (r2.dev or custom domain) allows public reads/listing of 'chat/', 'stores/<id>/proofs/', 'changelog/', 'backups/' prefixes. Keys are uuid4-unguessable and never serialized through non-private object_url calls (verified), so exposure requires key knowledge — but the bucket policy itself is a deployment fact not visible in source.
Production scheduling of purge_personal_data (cron/interval and --days value) — determines the real retention bound for chat attachments and whether the candidate's growth is annual or perpetual.

Production env state for S3_API/R2_* — determines whether local-fallback branches (chat private/, AI-design gallery /media/) are reachable and whether R2-only endpoints (proofs, changelog, feed) function at all; check_env coverage unverified in this pass.

Frontend iframe sandbox attributes for the pattern document (published web embed and 'Ver este diseño' srcdoc modal in the Vue SPA) — AGENTS.md documents sandbox without allow-same-origin, but the front-end code was outside this backend unit's reviewed paths.
Whether any CDN/reverse proxy in front of R2_PUBLIC_URL caches or re-serves objects with different ACL semantics than the bucket itself (e.g., Cloudflare cache rules on r2.dev/custom domain).
